validity.researcher_notes: P3601 is TC Energy/Tuscarora Gas Transmission Company's 'Tuscarora XPress Project', a FERC-authorized (Docket CP20-486, NGA sec.7(b)/7(c)) capacity expansion filed 2020-06-24 that replaced a 600-hp compressor with a 1,380-hp unit at the existing Wadsworth Compressor Station (Washoe County, NV) to add ~15,000 Dth/d of firm capacity from Malin, OR to Wadsworth, NV — no new pipe. This is a genuine, independently-documented project, not a GEM-only entity, not a duplicate of P0275 (the main Tuscarora system) or any other roster row, and correctly classified as gas transmission. EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: confirmed via (1) EIA's 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' workbook (Historical Projects tab, downloaded and read locally per the source ladder — a fully independent US-government statistical source), which carries this exact project as 'Tuscarora Xpress Project', Operator 'TC Energy', Project Type 'Expansion', Pipeline Type 'Interstate', Authority 'FERC', Docket 'CP20-486', Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2021-11-08, Year In Service 2021, Beg_State OR / End_State NV, Cost (millions) 13.45, Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) 15; and (2) three Federal Register notices in the same FERC docket (Notice of Application 2020-07-14/2020-15043; Notice of Intent to prepare an EA 2020-08-11/2020-17512; Notice of Schedule 2020-10-07/2020-22159), independently confirming the same scope, capacity (15,000 Dth/d), and Malin OR -> Wadsworth CS, Washoe County, NV routing. (3) TC Energy's own 'Tuscarora XPress Fact Sheet' (PDF, June 2020) gives the project schedule (Dec 2019 outreach, June 2020 file FERC application, June 2021 begin construction, Nov 2021 in-service) and confirms the scope is compressor replacement only, 'largely within the existing footprint.' EIA (independent) + FERC Federal Register (independent) + TC Energy fact sheet (operator) triangulate on every field on this row — see fills[] for the per-cell refs. VALUE CHECK: every recorded value (Capacity 15.00 MMcf/d, Length 0.00 km, Proposal 2020, Construction 2021, Start 2021, SegmentCost 13,450,000 USD) matches these sources exactly or within rounding (Capacity: 15,000 Dth/d ~ 15 MMcf/d given ~1,000-1,030 Btu/scf gas — EIA states 'Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) = 15' directly, an exact match; SegmentCost: EIA's 'Cost (millions) = 13.45' is an EXACT match to the sheet's 13,450,000 USD). DUPLICATE CHECK: not a duplicate of P0275 (Tuscarora main system, 305 mi/miscoded as 305 km — see cross_row_leads) or of any other roster row; P3601 is the correctly-modeled incremental capacity-expansion phase of the same physical system, the same pattern the sweep brief already confirms for P2517/P2569/P2614/P2615. SOURCES OPENED: 8 of the 9 harvested wiki citations were opened/tested (bit.ly wiki citation resolved to en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuscarora_Gas_Pipeline — no XPress-specific content there; tcenergy.com/.../tuscarora-transmission-system/ — live, system-level page; tcplus.com/Tuscarora — live, operator asset-facts page; offshore-technology.com/.../tuscarora-gas-pipeline-the-us/ — live, system-level description; ceqanet.opr.ca.gov/1993112055/2 — live, 1994 CEQA record for the ORIGINAL 1990s pipeline, not the XPress increment; tcenergy.com/.../tuscarora-xpress-project/ — now 404, dead; tcenergy.com fact sheet PDF — live, read in full; ferc.gov/media/c-3-cp20-486-000-052021 — 403 to a scripted client, but the same docket (CP20-486) is fully corroborated via the three Federal Register notices and the EIA workbook, so the finding does not depend on this one dead link). The 9th harvested citation, eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php, is a generic data hub (a mutable navigation surface, not independently citable per the source-ladder rule); I went straight to the specific dataset it points to — EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook — and read it locally, which is what actually supports the values below.

validity.recommendation: none — confirms the current Owner1 value; do not apply the batch brief's 'TC PipeLines LP is dissolved' premise to this pipeline
validity.researcher_notes: IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE BATCH-WIDE GUIDANCE for this pipeline specifically: the scope brief states 'TC PipeLines LP is a dissolved entity' following the March 2021 TC Energy/TC PipeLines LP merger, and flags Owner1='TC PipeLines LP [100%]' on P3601 (and P0275) as stale on that basis. That premise does not hold for Tuscarora. The 2021 merger took TC PipeLines, LP PRIVATE (TC Energy acquired all publicly-held common units and it stopped trading on Nasdaq as 'TCP'), but the LP itself was NOT dissolved — it continues to exist as a distinct, wholly-owned reporting entity. TC Energy's own 'TC PipeLines, LP Consolidated Financial Statements' for Q4 2024 (published 2025) and referenced again in the 2025 statements both list 'Tuscarora Gas Transmission Company (Tuscarora)' as one of TC PipeLines LP's owned systems at 100 percent, as recently as December 31, 2024. tcplus.com (Tuscarora's own regulatory-postings site) independently states 'TC PipeLines, LP owns 100 percent of Tuscarora.' So Owner1='TC PipeLines LP' at 100% is CURRENT and correct as recorded — no change needed. Caveat: both of my confirming sources are TC Energy/TC PipeLines corporate-family disclosures (the operator's own audited financials + its own subsidiary's customer portal), not a third-party-independent source; I searched for an independent (non-TC-Energy) confirmation of the post-2021 ownership structure (S&P/Moody's rating commentary, trade press) and did not find one within the time available, so I'm flagging this as tier=medium on independence grounds even though the two sources are about as authoritative as this kind of fact gets (a subsidiary's own audited financial statements). This finding does not necessarily generalize to other rows in the batch that also carry 'TC PipeLines LP' — each should be checked against TC PipeLines LP's own current financial statements before being changed.

FERC's Notice of Application (Federal Register 2020-07-14/2020-15043) is explicit: the project runs 'from Malin, Oregon to the Wadsworth Compressor Station (CS) in Washoe County, Nevada.' Likewise StartPrefecture/District is blank; Malin, Oregon sits in Klamath County (Wikipedia, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malin,_Oregon, and consistent with every gazetteer entry for the city). EIA's workbook independently corroborates the state-level termini (Beg_State=OR, End_State=NV). Net effect: the values on the sheet are directionally right, but the district/prefecture columns need the county names, and 'Wadsworth' needs to move from EndPrefecture/District to EndLocation.

cross_row_leads.facts: TC Energy's own system page states in its meta description: 'The 305-mile (491-km) Tuscarora Gas Transmission System...' — i.e., 305 MILES = 491 km. TC PipeLines LP's FY2024 financial statements (tcenergy.com PDF) independently state the same figure in a route table: 'Tuscarora 305 miles Extends between the GTN pipeline near Malin, Oregon to its terminus near Reno, Nevada.' offshore-technology.com corroborates with '491km-long Tuscarora gas pipeline ... maximum diameter of 20 inches.' P0275's roster entry here shows LengthKnown=305.0 with LengthKnownUnits='km' — that looks like a mile figure mislabeled as kilometres (305 mi ~= 491 km, not 305 km). Worth a validity check on P0275 specifically: either LengthKnownUnits should read 'mi' (leaving LengthKnown=305.0), or LengthKnown should be corrected to ~491 (km). Also note: the same offshore-technology.com source gives P0275 a maximum diameter of 20 inches, which may be a useful Diameter ref for that row if it currently lacks one.
